question: When you key a property on a video, should the picture shrink to make room for the new key lane?
context: Measured on 2026-10-07 in animate-pick-cost-walk: the picture reads 74% before Position is keyed, 71% after, 74% again after Undo. A key and its undo both hold the app about 70 ms; keeping the timeline height was measured by an earlier runner at about 7 ms less per key and undo (undo near 55 ms).

options.label: Timeline grows, picture shrinks a little
options.summary: As today: picking Position from Animate a property opens a key lane under the clip, the timeline grows by one lane and the picture above it shrinks from 74% to 71%. Undo grows it back.
pros: Every track stays in view without scrolling the timeline
cons: The picture jumps on every first key and every undo of it
Keying a value and undoing it each take about 70 ms, over the 50 ms the video goals ask for
options.mitigation: A later task could animate the resize so the jump reads as motion, but that adds frames rather than removing work.

options.label: Timeline keeps its height, picture stays put
options.summary: Picking Position opens the key lane inside the timeline as it is: the tracks under it move down and the timeline scrolls if they no longer fit. The picture never changes size when you key or undo.
pros: The picture you are animating never moves under your pointer
Matches Premiere and Final Cut, where keyframing never resizes the program monitor
About 7 ms less per key and per undo, measured on 2026-10-07
cons: On a short timeline, the bottom track can slide out of view until you scroll or drag the divider up
options.mitigation: The timeline already scrolls and its divider already drags; the lane only takes room while a key exists.
